steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on CycleNet, a method for unpaired image-to-image translation with pre-trained text-guided diffusion models using cycle consistency. Motivate why consistency matters, describe the method briefly, and summarize the new dataset and results.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Pre-trained diffusion models and I2I translation; limits of current approaches
2. Why consistency matters in unpaired I2I
3. CycleNet: method overview
4. Evaluation, ManiCups dataset, and main results

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Background and gap
- pre-trained diffusion models (DMs): breakthrough in image synthesis (cite)
- vs GANs (cite), VAEs (cite): better stability and quality, can scale to open-world multi-modal data
- applied to image-to-image (I2I) translation: mapping between images of two domains (scenes, objects, object states)
- text-guided DMs need mask layers (cite) or attention control (cite)
- masks / attention maps unpredictable in complex scenes -> unwanted semantic and structural changes
- paired I2I with extra image-conditioning: side network (cite), adapter (cite)
- open challenge: adapt pre-trained DMs to unpaired I2I with consistency guarantee

2. Consistency
- desirable in image manipulation; especially important in unpaired I2I (no guaranteed correspondence between source and target)
- applications relying on it: video prediction and infilling (cite), imagination-augmented language understanding (cite), robotic manipulation (cite), world models (cite)

3. CycleNet
- unpaired I2I with pre-trained DMs; conditions on input image and text prompts
- ControlNet (cite) + pre-trained Stable Diffusion (SD) (cite) as latent DM backbone
- motivated by cycle consistency in GAN-based methods (cite); consistency regularization over translation cycle
- Figure 2: forward x_{0} -> \bar{y}_{0}, backward -> \bar{x}_{0}
- key idea: conditioned on image c_{\mathrm{img}} in target domain given by c_{\mathrm{text}}, DM should reproduce the image condition through reverse process

4. Experiments and results
- I2I tasks of different granularities; scene and object level tasks from prior work (cite)
- new dataset ManiCups: multi-domain, physical state changes of objects; 6k images of empty cups and cups of coffee, juice, milk, water; from human-annotated bounding boxes
- better than previous approaches: translation faithfulness, cycle consistency, image quality
- computationally friendly: robust with very limited data (around 2k), minimal resources (1 GPU)
- robust zero-shot I2I translator: out-of-domain, simple change of text prompt
- opens up consistent diffusion-based image manipulation with image conditioning + free-form language instructions

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Pre-trained diffusion models (DMs) have recently made a big breakthrough in image synthesis. DMs are more stable and give better quality images than GANs and VAEs, and they can also be scaled up to open-world multi-modal data. Because of this, pre-trained DMs have been used for image-to-image (I2I) translation, which means learning a mapping between images from two different domains, e.g., different scenes, different objects, and different object states. To do these translations, text-guided diffusion models usually need mask layers or attention control. But the masks and attention maps can be of unpredictable quality in complex scenes, and this leads to semantic and structural changes that we do not want. Researchers have recently tried using additional image-conditioning for paired I2I translations, with a side network or an adapter. However, how to adapt pre-trained DMs to unpaired I2I translation with a consistency guarantee is still an open challenge.

Consistency is a desirable property in image manipulation, and it is especially important in unpaired I2I, because in that setting there is no guaranteed correspondence between the images in the source domain and the target domain. Many applications of DMs would need strong consistency between the source and the generated images, for example video prediction and infilling, imagination-augmented language understanding, robotic manipulation and world models.

3. CycleNet
- unpaired I2I with pre-trained DMs; conditions on input image and text prompts
- ControlNet + pre-trained Stable Diffusion (SD) as latent DM backbone
- motivated by cycle consistency in GAN-based methods; consistency regularization over translation cycle
- Figure 2: forward x_{0} -> \bar{y}_{0}, backward -> \bar{x}_{0}
- key idea: conditioned on c_{\mathrm{img}} in target domain given by c_{\mathrm{text}}, DM should reproduce the image condition through reverse process

4. Experiments and results
- I2I tasks of different granularities; scene and object level tasks from earlier work
- ManiCups: multi-domain, physical state changes of objects; 6k images of empty cups and cups of coffee, juice, milk, water; human-annotated bounding boxes
- better faithfulness, cycle consistency, image quality than previous approaches
- robust with very limited data (around 2k), minimal resources (1 GPU)
- robust zero-shot I2I translator for out-of-domain distributions by changing the prompt
- opens up consistent diffusion-based image manipulation with image conditioning + free-form language instructions

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Pre-trained diffusion models (DMs) have recently made a big breakthrough in image synthesis. DMs are more stable and give better quality images than GANs and VAEs, and they can also be scaled up to open-world multi-modal data. Because of this, pre-trained DMs have been used for image-to-image (I2I) translation, which means learning a mapping between images from two different domains, e.g., different scenes, different objects, and different object states. To do these translations, text-guided diffusion models usually need mask layers or attention control. But the masks and attention maps can be of unpredictable quality in complex scenes, and this leads to semantic and structural changes that we do not want. Researchers have recently tried using additional image-conditioning for paired I2I translations, with a side network or an adapter. However, how to adapt pre-trained DMs to unpaired I2I translation with a consistency guarantee is still an open challenge.

Consistency is a desirable property in image manipulation, and it is especially important in unpaired I2I, because in that setting there is no guaranteed correspondence between the images in the source domain and the target domain. Many applications of DMs would need strong consistency between the source and the generated images, for example video prediction and infilling, imagination-augmented language understanding, robotic manipulation and world models.

In this paper we introduce CycleNet to make unpaired I2I translation with pre-trained DMs possible with good consistency. CycleNet lets DMs translate a source image by conditioning on the input image and on text prompts. We use ControlNet with pre-trained Stable Diffusion (SD) as the latent DM backbone. Motivated by cycle consistency in GAN-based methods, CycleNet uses consistency regularization over the image translation cycle. The image translation cycle (see Figure 2) has a forward translation from x_{0} to \bar{y}_{0} and a backward translation to \bar{x}_{0}. The key idea is that when the DM is conditioned on an image c_{\mathrm{img}} that is in the target domain given by c_{\mathrm{text}}, it should be able to reproduce this image condition through the reverse process.

We test CycleNet on I2I translation tasks of different granularities. Besides the scene and object level tasks introduced by earlier work, we also contribute a new dataset, ManiCups, which is a multi-domain I2I translation dataset for manipulating physical state changes of objects. ManiCups has 6k images of empty cups and cups of coffee, juice, milk, and water, which were collected from human-annotated bounding boxes. The results show that CycleNet is better than previous approaches in translation faithfulness, cycle consistency, and image quality. The approach is also computationally friendly: it is robust even with very limited training data (around 2k) and needs minimal computational resources (1 GPU) to train. Further analysis shows that CycleNet is a robust zero-shot I2I translator, and it can generate faithful and high-quality images for out-of-domain distributions just by changing the textual prompt. This opens up possibilities for consistent diffusion-based image manipulation models with image conditioning and free-form language instructions.

steps.name: cited_draft
steps.text:
Pre-trained diffusion models (DMs) [1,2,3] have recently made a big breakthrough in image synthesis. DMs are more stable and give better quality images than GANs [4] and VAEs [5], and they can also be scaled up to open-world multi-modal data. Because of this, pre-trained DMs have been used for image-to-image (I2I) translation, which means learning a mapping between images from two different domains, e.g., different scenes, different objects, and different object states. To do these translations, text-guided diffusion models usually need mask layers [6,7,8,9] or attention control [10,11,12,13]. But the masks and attention maps can be of unpredictable quality in complex scenes, and this leads to semantic and structural changes that we do not want. Researchers have recently tried using additional image-conditioning for paired I2I translations, with a side network [14] or an adapter [15]. However, how to adapt pre-trained DMs to unpaired I2I translation with a consistency guarantee is still an open challenge.

Consistency is a desirable property in image manipulation, and it is especially important in unpaired I2I, because in that setting there is no guaranteed correspondence between the images in the source domain and the target domain. Many applications of DMs would need strong consistency between the source and the generated images, for example video prediction and infilling [16], imagination-augmented language understanding [17], robotic manipulation [18,19] and world models [20].

In this paper we introduce CycleNet to make unpaired I2I translation with pre-trained DMs possible with good consistency. CycleNet lets DMs translate a source image by conditioning on the input image and on text prompts. We use ControlNet [14] with pre-trained Stable Diffusion (SD) [1] as the latent DM backbone. Motivated by cycle consistency in GAN-based methods [21], CycleNet uses consistency regularization over the image translation cycle. The image translation cycle (see Figure 2) has a forward translation from x_{0} to \bar{y}_{0} and a backward translation to \bar{x}_{0}. The key idea is that when the DM is conditioned on an image c_{\mathrm{img}} that is in the target domain given by c_{\mathrm{text}}, it should be able to reproduce this image condition through the reverse process.

We test CycleNet on I2I translation tasks of different granularities. Besides the scene and object level tasks introduced by [21], we also contribute a new dataset, ManiCups, which is a multi-domain I2I translation dataset for manipulating physical state changes of objects. ManiCups has 6k images of empty cups and cups of coffee, juice, milk, and water, which were collected from human-annotated bounding boxes. The results show that CycleNet is better than previous approaches in translation faithfulness, cycle consistency, and image quality. The approach is also computationally friendly: it is robust even with very limited training data (around 2k) and needs minimal computational resources (1 GPU) to train. Further analysis shows that CycleNet is a robust zero-shot I2I translator, and it can generate faithful and high-quality images for out-of-domain distributions just by changing the textual prompt. This opens up possibilities for consistent diffusion-based image manipulation models with image conditioning and free-form language instructions.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Recently, pre-trained diffusion models (DMs) [1,2,3] have enabled an unprecedented breakthrough in image synthesis tasks. Compared to GANs [4] and VAEs [5], DMs show superior stability and quality in image generation, and they can scale up to open-world multi-modal data. As such, pre-trained DMs have been applied to image-to-image (I2I) translation, which is to acquire a mapping between images from two distinct domains, e.g., different scenes, different objects, and different object states. For such translations, text-guided diffusion models typically require mask layers [6,7,8,9] or attention control [10,11,12,13]. However, the quality of masks and attention maps can be unpredictable in complex scenes, which leads to undesirable semantic and structural changes. Recently, researchers have explored additional image-conditioning to perform paired I2I translations with the help of a side network [14] or an adapter [15]. Still, it remains an open challenge to adapt pre-trained DMs in unpaired I2I translation with a consistency guarantee.

We emphasize that consistency, a desirable property in image manipulation, is particularly important in unpaired I2I scenarios, where there is no guaranteed correspondence between images in the source and target domains. Various applications of DMs, including video prediction and infilling [16], imagination-augmented language understanding [17], robotic manipulation [18,19] and world models [20], would rely on strong consistency across the source and generated images.

To enable unpaired I2I translation using pre-trained DMs with satisfactory consistency, this paper introduces CycleNet, which allows DMs to translate a source image by conditioning on the input image and text prompts. Specifically, we adopt ControlNet [14] with pre-trained Stable Diffusion (SD) [1] as the latent DM backbone. Motivated by cycle consistency in GAN-based methods [21], CycleNet applies consistency regularization over the image translation cycle. As illustrated in Figure 2, the cycle includes a forward translation from x_{0} to \bar{y}_{0} and a backward translation to \bar{x}_{0}. The key idea of our method is that when conditioned on an image c_{\mathrm{img}} that falls into the target domain specified by c_{\mathrm{text}}, the DM should be able to reproduce this image condition through the reverse process.

We validate CycleNet on I2I translation tasks of different granularities. Besides the scene and object level tasks introduced by [21], we additionally contribute ManiCups, a multi-domain I2I translation dataset for manipulating physical state changes of objects. ManiCups contains 6k images of empty cups and cups of coffee, juice, milk, and water, collected from human-annotated bounding boxes. Empirical results show that, compared to previous approaches, CycleNet is superior in translation faithfulness, cycle consistency, and image quality. Our approach is also computationally friendly: it is robust even with very limited training data (around 2k) and requires minimal computational resources (1 GPU) to train. Further analysis shows that CycleNet is a robust zero-shot I2I translator that can generate faithful and high-quality images for out-of-domain distributions with a simple change of the textual prompt. This opens up possibilities for developing consistent diffusion-based image manipulation models with image conditioning and free-form language instructions.
